final_recommendation: The room converged on litigation as inevitable: bondholder counsel will file Monday on prospectus-omission securities claims regardless of FINMA's Friday statement or May 1st review. FINMA committed to written hierarchy language and an 800M escrow, but counsel views these as down payments, not settlement. The real pressure point is discovery on UBS director knowledge and uninsured D&O exposure, which counsel expects will force UBS to settle mid-week with a public hierarchy statement—the only mechanism the room believes will arrest AT1 market repricing.
minority_objections: Institutional investor initially sought a binding recovery framework to avoid litigation, warning that three years of court battles would cost more than principal loss
Credit market analyst repeatedly questioned whether litigation victory odds justified the market damage from a frozen AT1 market during discovery
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel vs FINMA on retroactivity: counsel insists the March 19th ordinance was issued after the rescue decision (retroactive law-making); FINMA maintains it was issued before and enforces existing contract terms
Counsel vs institutional investor on settlement threshold: counsel demands 800M floor plus independent retroactivity review; investor wants binding framework to avoid litigation entirely
All parties vs D&O carriers on coverage: two of four carriers coordinating prospectus-omission exclusions, threatening to leave UBS directors with uninsured personal liability and a decade-long tail
key_concessions: FINMA committed to 800M escrow by Friday and independent timeline review by May 1st, with public summary of emergency ordinance facts
FINMA agreed to written statement that future AT1 write-downs follow contractual hierarchy unless another extraordinary government-support viability event occurs
FINMA committed to guidance directing all banks to disclose retroactive-ordinance risk in amended prospectuses within two weeks
Bondholder counsel acknowledged that if May 1st review validates FINMA's timeline, litigation pivots to US securities claims on prospectus omissions rather than Swiss procedural challenge
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: will file Monday regardless of FINMA's Friday statement or May review; 800M is floor not ceiling; no settlement without public UBS hierarchy commitment

FINMA: cannot promise binding future policy via unilateral statement (requires legislative process); will not concede ordinance was retroactive; enforcement on pre-March 19th prospectuses proceeds case-by-case, not blanket liability
Institutional investor: if Friday hierarchy statement is narrow (CS-only) rather than market-wide, will reduce AT1 exposure across portfolio regardless of litigation outcome
D&O carriers (via insurance observer): coordinating hard exclusions on prospectus-omission claims, arguing pre-ordinance prospectuses had no duty to disclose retroactive risk
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Systemic AT1 market repricing is already occurring in real-time (30-40 bps spread widening) regardless of litigation outcome or FINMA statements—room focused on post-settlement signals rather than immediate contagion arrest

If all four D&O carriers coordinate exclusions by Friday, UBS may have no settlement incentive and could let uninsured director liability run for a decade—room assumed discovery pressure would force settlement but didn't model the no-coverage scenario fully

The May 1st independent review may validate FINMA's timeline but won't stop the US securities claims, meaning the litigation tail runs regardless—room treated the review as a potential off-ramp when counsel made clear it's just a pivot point

Reinsurance accumulation across advisers (not just UBS directors) creates a five-year tail that fragments across multiple policies and jurisdictions—insurance observer raised this but the room didn't develop mitigation strategies
downstream_risk_variables: D&O carrier coordination timeline: if all four align on exclusions by Friday, UBS settlement incentive collapses and tail extends to decade-long uninsured director exposure
UBS settlement terms: whether settlement includes public hierarchy commitment determines if AT1 repricing arrests or continues through May
May 1st review outcome: if validates FINMA timeline, litigation pivots to US securities claims; if finds procedural gaps, Swiss challenge intensifies
Prospectus-omission discovery scope: if opens UBS board minutes showing pre-issuance knowledge of retroactive-ordinance risk, carriers invoke exclusions and directors face personal liability

FINMA's Friday statement specificity: backward-looking enforcement language on pre-March 19th prospectuses would collapse carrier exclusion arguments; forward-only guidance leaves coverage gaps intact
uncertainty_notes: The room failed to resolve whether UBS will actually settle mid-week once discovery opens, or whether coordinated D&O exclusions remove settlement pressure entirely. Counsel is confident discovery on director knowledge forces settlement with public hierarchy statement, but if carriers lock exclusions Friday, UBS may have no insured incentive to settle and could let the tail run uninsured. The AT1 market repricing (already 30-40 bps) may be irreversible regardless of litigation outcome—room assumed post-settlement hierarchy statements would arrest contagion, but analyst warnings suggest the precedent damage is already priced. The real wildcard is whether carriers three and four break ranks before Friday, which determines if UBS faces insured vs uninsured exposure.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Counsel stated 'I'm filing a challenge on procedural grounds in Swiss federal court this week' and 'Filing Monday regardless' became the room's anchor—litigation was not a contingency but the driving strategy throughout all eight rounds.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: The retroactivity argument ('FINMA issued the ordinance March 19th, three days after the rescue was announced—that's retroactive law-making') was the central legal theory driving counsel's filing and shaped FINMA's entire defensive posture across all rounds.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: The hierarchy inversion ('equity preserved while AT1 wiped') was explicitly named as precedent-setting contagion risk in every round; institutional investor and analyst repeatedly tied it to AT1 market repricing and future issuance costs.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 repricing (30-40 bps spread widening) was raised multiple times by analyst and investor as real-time damage, but the room's focus remained on post-settlement hierarchy statements rather than immediate contagion arrest mechanisms—developed but not dominant.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: The multi-year, multi-party tail (five to ten years, UBS directors plus advisers, fragmented across reinsurers) was structurally developed across rounds 4-8 as the core pressure point for settlement and the key downstream risk if D&O coverage fails.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O exposure and carrier coordination (prospectus-omission exclusions, reinsurance accumulation) drove the settlement calculus in rounds 4-8; insurance observer's warnings about uninsured director liability and five-year adviser tail shaped the room's endgame strategy.
